**(B)** carbohydrate.

The exoskeleton of cockroach is made of chitin, a nitrogenous polysaccharide, so chemically it is a carbohydrate. It contains nitrogen because its sugar units carry amino groups, but it is not a protein, a lipid or a glycoprotein.

**(B)** chewing and biting

Cockroach is omnivorous, and its mouthparts (labrum, mandibles, maxillae, labium and hypopharynx) are of the chewing and biting type; the hard, serrated mandibles cut and crush the food. Sponging mouthparts are found in the housefly, piercing and sucking in the female mosquito and bedbug, and lapping (with chewing) in the honey bee.

**(B)** respiration

Spiracles are the paired respiratory openings of the cockroach, two pairs on the thorax and eight on the abdomen. They let air into and out of the tracheae of the tracheal (respiratory) system. They have no role in circulation, reproduction or nerve conduction.

**(B)** Hypopharynx

The hypopharynx (tongue) is one of the mouthparts; the salivary duct opens at its base, and it helps mix saliva with food, so it belongs to the digestive system. The trachea belongs to the respiratory system, haemocytes are cells of the haemolymph (circulatory system), and the seminal vesicle is part of the male reproductive system.

**(A)** Supra-oesophageal ganglion

The pair of supra-oesophageal (cerebral) ganglia, lying in the head above the oesophagus between the antennal bases, is collectively called the brain. The sub-oesophageal ganglion lies below the oesophagus, the hypocerebral ganglion is part of the autonomous nervous system, and the thoracic ganglia are segmental ganglia of the ventral nerve cord.
